### Bible Pathways - June 17, 2005
Author: Bible Pathways
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-june-17-2005-1335238.html
Passage: Job 9:32-33
Points:
- Suffering is not proof of personal wrongdoing, contrary to the assumptions of Job's friends.
- Job acknowledged the absolute sovereignty and greatness of God over mortal humanity.
- A human cannot summon God to trial or debate Him on equal footing.
- Job expressed a desperate longing for an arbiter who could lay a hand on both parties.
- Jesus Christ serves as the ultimate Mediator who bridges the divide and reconciles humanity to God.

### PowerPoint - May 7, 2009
Author: Jack Graham
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/powerpoint/powerpoint-may-7-2009-11603271.html
Passage: Job 9:2
Points:
- Job raises humanity's most critical question: how a mortal can be right before God.
- No amount of human effort, good deeds, or religion can achieve righteousness.
- True standing before God comes solely through the gift of divine grace.
- Believers are forgiven and declared righteous through faith in Jesus Christ.
- Daily life should be marked by ongoing thanksgiving for Christ's sacrifice.
